data.title: Fed's Barr worried regulatory changes may increase financial sector risks
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Thursday that US financial regulation changes underway at the central bank could make it harder to identify and respond to future market troubles. 

Barr had been the Fed's top financial supervision official until early 2025, at the beginning of President Donald Trump's second term, when he gave up the role in what he said was an effort to preserve Fed independence.

His successor, Michelle Bowman, has pursued a deregulation effort that aims to increase accountability, but which has raised concerns about gaps in oversight. 

"I'm not worried about it in a today sense," but these changes "are things that have longer term tails to them, longer term consequences, and so there can be a gradual weakening over time in supervision" that makes the banking system less safe, Barr said at the FinRegLab 2026 AI Symposium.

Barr said that around a third of Fed bank regulator jobs in Washington are on the chopping block, adding that, during the 2007-2009 global financial crisis, the central bank lacked sufficient talent on its staff that could quickly identify and understand problems. 

Those changes alongside others "add up," he said. "Not any one of them is ... a risk tomorrow, but ... I think there are risks worth worrying about." 

Barr added that he has been "very public" about his disagreements with "the direction of travel" in Fed supervision and regulation over the last year and a half.  

Turning to monetary policy, Barr repeated that he believes the Fed will need to raise interest rates again. "Inflation is too high," he said, "so I think we're going to need to adjust monetary policy further." 

The Fed next meets on December 8 and 9, when it is expected to increase its current 3.75% to 4% interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point. It is expected to hike again in the new year as it works to lower price pressures. 

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Jonathan Spicer )

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI fervor
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US stocks slumped on Thursday, after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revitalize faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.

Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 a share and quickly rose as high as $115 a share, or 38.6% above the offer price, but pared those gains to 17.1% by the end of the session.

All three major US stock indexes dropped at least 2%, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its sixth straight session of losses.

The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly decline since April 2025.

Anthropic's debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced late Wednesday at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened shortly before noon. After the company's market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began to lose steam.

"The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri. "That money is coming from somewhere; investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from today's trading behavior, whether it's up or down."

Even so, Ellerbroek's enthusiasm for the AI trade has waned.

"My beliefs about the growth in data center capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two," he added. "Nvidia's ( NVDA ) crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact."

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly."

Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares tumbled 7.7% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most tech stocks lost ground, with Micron and Broadcom ( AVGO ) both dropping 2.1%.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) declined 3.3%, its sixth straight losing session, after the chipmaker's upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed 2.4% lower on the day.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) dropped 6.1% and Nebius slid 9.4%.

The broader technology sector ended down 1.9%.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped 6.4% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance.

Walmart ( WMT ) slipped 1.0% following the retail giant's disappointing annual sales forecast.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, the S&P 500 lost 147.80 points, or 2.02%, to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 550.68 points, or 2.25%, to 23,879.20.

FOCUS TURNS TO THE FED

Following Wednesday's release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in a 96.4% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the central bank's December meeting, with a small chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above the central bank's 2% annual target.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4.37-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 21 new highs and 796 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,057 stocks rose and 3,756 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.55-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted one new 52-week high and 18 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 34 new highs and 529 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 20.83 billion shares, compared with the 19.00 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

(Reporting by Stephen Culp; Additional reporting by Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gregorio)

data.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months, committee says
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday. 

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies, the committee noted.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China.

Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million chips to China total during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Jensen Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech ​threats.

"The fact that over 30% of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese Military Companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses," said Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle.

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."

AMD, Alibaba ( BABA ), Tencent ( TCTZF ), Baidu ( BIDU ), BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

MOST DETAILED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE   

Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence.

But President Donald Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum.

Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores.

In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place. In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few'. Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

 "This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee chair Brian Mast said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper, Ryan Patrick Jones, Katharine Jackson; Additional Reporting by David Shepardson editing by Scott Malone and Chris Sanders)

data.title: Anthropic's blockbuster debut tests Wall Street's faith in AI boom
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

The early exuberance faded, however, signaling volatility ahead as investors locked in quick gains and the main indexes retreated amid renewed jitters over the sector's outlook.

Shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company opened at $111.50, which was 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and ended the day at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

Anthropic's fully diluted $2 trillion valuation includes stock options and restricted stock units that the company has promised employees but which have not been vested into actual shares. Based on Anthropic's outstanding shares, the company's value reached as much as $1.5 trillion on Thursday, on par with Tesla.

The AI market euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks, with last week's resignation of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang causing concern. The technology has boosted economic growth but has prompted unease about mounting debt loads and doomsday warnings. An anti-data-center movement may have helped Democrats sweep the US midterm elections.

"The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," said Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. "We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia ( NVDA ) situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability."

The six-year-old company has positioned itself as the gatekeeper of AI safety while selling investors the idea that it can be profitable despite massive compute costs. Led by Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has also signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Amodei told CNBC in an interview on Thursday.

Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from the previous quarter, even as the pace of growth slowed sharply from the prior quarter. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google.

INDUSTRY BENCHMARK, EMPLOYEE PAYDAY

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show.

Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for the purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

Based on the IPO price, Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified over whether the AI boom is becoming a bubble as soaring valuations and a web of circular deals involving AI developers, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors fuel questions about the durability of the industry's growth.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far insulated it from these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

Anthropic "isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," said Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group. "History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon."

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

The massive IPO will earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

By Anand Gopal R and Fergal Smith

TORONTO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Canada's main stock index fell for a sixth straight day to hit a six-month low on Thursday as a selloff in gold extended, with metal mining and technology shares pacing broad-based declines.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended down 549.32 points, or 1.6%, at 34,028.73, its lowest closing level since May 19. The daily losing streak was the longest since December 2024.

* Gold fell 1.6% to a 14-month low as it continued to face pressure from US dollar strength, with markets fully pricing in an interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, owing to stubborn inflation.

* "There was this over-excitement in gold and copper and commodity stocks, and now the air is coming out of that trade or those investments," said Matt Manara, executive vice president and portfolio manager at Avenue Investment Management.

* The materials sector, which includes metal mining shares, fell 2.9%. Shares of Seabridge Gold ( SA ) tumbled 29.3% to the lowest closing level since September 2025.

* US stocks also posted steep declines as Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revive faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence.

* The TSX's technology sector lost 3.3%, with shares of e-commerce company Shopify ( SHOP ) falling 5.2%.

* Canada's banking regulator proposed regulatory changes to level the playing field between the country's dominant lenders and smaller banks and credit unions, in a push to increase competition in the sector.

* Heavily weighted financials and energy both ended 1% lower.

* US crude oil futures settled down 0.1% at $83.21 a barrel as the prospect of surplus supply offset fresh reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

* All the major sectors traded in negative territory.

* Telus ( TU ), the target of a Quebecor ( QBCAF ) takeover proposal, was a bright spot. Its shares rose 13.7% after a report that BCE has held preliminary discussions with the company.

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI fervor
data.description:
* Anthropic briefly hits $2 trillion in market value

* Walmart ( WMT ) dips after forecasting annual sales below estimates

* Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) lifts FY27 forecast

(Updates to market close)

By Stephen Culp and Ragini Mathur

NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US stocks slumped on Thursday, after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revitalize faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.

All three major US stock indexes ended the session sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses.

The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly loss since April 2025.

Anthropic's debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced late Wednesday at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly before noon. After the company's market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began to lose steam.

"The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri. "That money is coming from somewhere; investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from today's trading behavior, whether it's up or down."

Even so, Ellerbroek's enthusiasm for the AI trade has waned.

"My beliefs about the growth in data center capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two," he added. "Nvidia's ( NVDA ) crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact."

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly."

Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares tumbled after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most chipmakers were lower, including Micron and Broadcom ( AVGO ), among others.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) marked its sixth straight session of losses after the chipmaker's upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed lower.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius sustained steep losses.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance.

Walmart ( WMT ) dipped after the retail giant's annual sales forecast disappointed investors.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 148.39 points, or 2.03%, to end at 7,175.24 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 544.00 points, or 2.23%, to 23,885.88. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,102.71 points, or 2.20%, to 49,095.46.

FOCUS TURNS TO THE FED

Following Wednesday's release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in about a 94% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the central bank's December meeting, with a small but growing chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above the central bank's 2% annual target.

(Reporting by Stephen Culp; Additional reporting by Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gregorio)

data.title: Exclusive-US should restrict investments in China's aerospace sector, not certify Chinese aircraft, lawmakers say
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government should refuse to certify Chinese-made airplanes and pull taxpayer contracts from American defense contractors including European aerospace manufacturer Airbus if they do not halt investments in China's aerospace industrial base, a congressional report seen by Reuters said.

The House Select Committee on China in a report said Washington should toughen export controls and restrict investments in China's aerospace sector. The report raised serious concerns that western governments did not do enough to contain the swift rise of China's military air power.

"The broader system allowed commercial aerospace engagement that could strengthen firms connected to the PRC's military industrial base without triggering the safeguards designed to protect sensitive technology," the report said following a year-long investigation.

Airbus declined to comment.

The report said the Federal Aviation Administration should not allow Chinese-manufactured aircraft to fly in the United States, noting that China has never released its report into the 2022 crash of a China Eastern Airlines Boeing aircraft and citing subsidies that China has given to state-owned Chinese airplane makers COMAC and AVIC. 

The Treasury Department should restrict outbound investment into China's aerospace sector and urge allies to follow suit and subject the purchase of US aerospace companies by French firms to heightened scrutiny until they unwind ties to China's "Civil-Military Ecosystem."

The report said through joint ventures, co-development agreements, and other commercial relationships "American and other Western companies transferred technology, know-how, and industrial capacity" on aerospace that ultimately benefited the Chinese military.

The report also found Honeywell Aerospace, GE Aerospace, and Collins Aerospace "repeatedly sought and obtained licenses for controlled technology transfers involving PRC military end users and other military-linked entities as part of Chinese commercial aerospace platforms."

Honeywell said all of the projects were "fully licensed and approved by the US government. Honeywell Aerospace has and will continue to follow all U.S. export laws and procedures, as is acknowledged in the report."

GE Aerospace said it "takes national security, compliance, and the protection of its intellectual property seriously, and we work closely with the US government.

The FAA and Collins Aerospace, a unit of RTX did not immediately comment.

The report also warned that "unilateral US restrictions would disadvantage American aerospace companies without denying China access to many Western technologies when allied firms backfill the resulting business."

The report said some French companies advertise themselves to Chinese customers as being beyond the reach of US restrictions and said Airbus advertises that it can sell satellite photos without US restrictions.

The report also said French aerospace companies "maintain much stronger ties to the Chinese aerospace industrial base than American companies" and called for a Treasury-led committee to "apply stricter scrutiny to French acquisitions of key American technology until France unwinds its close integration with the Chinese industrial base."

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: InterScripts and Children's Nebraska Earn 2026 CHIME Collaboration Award for AdaptCare
data.description:
CHANTILLY, Va., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- InterScripts, Inc., a healthcare IT services and software company, today announced that it has received the 2026 CHIME Collaboration Award together with Children's Nebraska from the College of Healthcare Information Management Executives (CHIME). The award was presented at the CHIME26 Fall Forum, held November 11–14 at the Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center in Aurora, Colorado, and recognizes the two organizations' joint development of AdaptCare, a patient care platform that gives emergency responders instant access to a child's individualized care plan.

The CHIME Collaboration Award is presented jointly to a CHIME member organization and a CHIME Foundation firm in recognition of a collaborative effort that delivers value to the healthcare IT community, both in the quality of the partnership and in the significance of the work itself. It is one of the few industry honors that recognizes a health system and its technology partner together rather than separately.

Built With Clinicians for the Children Who Need It Most

 AdaptCare grew out of Children's Nebraska's Project Austin program, which develops individualized emergency care plans for children with medical complexity so emergency responders and emergency department teams understand each child's unique medical and communication needs before providing care. Working directly with the program's nurse founders, InterScripts designed and built a secure mobile and web platform that integrates with the hospital's electronic health record and delivers each child's care plan, communication needs, and treatment precautions to first responders at the point of care, even when a parent or guardian is not present.

The platform provides responders with important information about a child's individual needs, including communication preferences, sensory sensitivities, medical conditions and medications that may affect emergency treatment. Because EMTs, firefighters, and other responders are typically not credentialed at the hospital, AdaptCare closes a long-standing information gap between the health system and the first responders who reach a child first.

Children's Nebraska has reported that the program has contributed to a 27% reduction in hospital admissions, a 50% decrease in overall hospital length of stay, and a 55% reduction in cost across organizational services for enrolled patients. InterScripts now hosts, supports, and continues to develop AdaptCare, with Children's Nebraska as its founding clinical partner, and is making the platform available to additional children's hospitals and health systems.

"Innovation is a core value at Children's Nebraska, and Project Austin shows what that value looks like in practice. Two of our nurses saw that first responders needed to know how to care for our most medically complex kids before they reached the hospital, and they set out to fix it. InterScripts listened to our clinicians, embraced that innovation, and turned their idea into AdaptCare, a platform our community relies on every day, with results we can measure. Real innovation happens when a health system and a technology partner build something together, and this award recognizes exactly that." — Ryan M. Cameron, EVP, Chief Information & Innovation Officer, Children's Nebraska

The collaboration reflects InterScripts' approach to working with health systems: clinicians define the need, InterScripts engineers the solution, and both organizations share accountability for the outcome. The AdaptCare partnership has been showcased at HIMSS, and Children's Nebraska has been recognized by CHIME in consecutive years, including the inaugural CHIME & KLAS Synergy Award in 2024 and the CHIME Innovator of the Year Award in 2025.

"AdaptCare exists because two nurses at Children's Nebraska refused to accept that a child's care plan should stay locked inside the hospital walls. Our team's job was to bring that clinical intent to life in software that works at the roadside, in an ambulance, and in the emergency department. That is what innovation in healthcare looks like to us: it starts with clinicians who see a gap, and it succeeds when a partner is willing to engineer the solution alongside them and measure the results together. Being recognized by CHIME alongside Children's Nebraska is especially meaningful because the award honors the collaboration itself, and that is how we believe healthcare technology should be built." — Raju Togi, Founder, President & CEO, InterScripts, Inc.

Health systems interested in bringing AdaptCare to their communities, or in learning more about InterScripts' clinical application development, BytePad archival, Epic, and service desk capabilities, can visit www.interscripts.com.

Founded in 2017, InterScripts helps health systems retire legacy applications, preserve data integrity, and maintain access to historical records, and it develops and supports AdaptCare, a patient care platform built in partnership with Children's Nebraska. data.title: Diversified Energy Completes Birch Acquisition
data.description:
Diversified Energy Company ( DEC ) (“Diversified” or the “Company”) announces the close, on November 19, 2026, of its previously announced, accretive acquisition of Birch Permian Holdings, Inc. and certain affiliated companies (collectively, “Birch”) from its former owners (the “Sellers”) (the “Acquisition”). The Acquisition adds complementary operated producing properties and acreage positions in the Permian Basin (the “Assets”). In conjunction with the closing of the Acquisition, the Company closed on a $1,455 million asset backed securitization (“ABS XIV”), TCG Capital Markets L.L.C. served as Sole Structuring Agent and Sole Placement Agent on the financing. CIBC Capital Markets provided an LC Liquidity Facility to meet the liquidity reserve requirements.

Rusty Hutson, Jr., Chairman and CEO of Diversified, commented:

"We are excited to announce the closing of Birch, which delivers high-quality producing assets, durable cash flow, and a contiguous Permian Basin position. This highly accretive acquisition is exactly the type of transaction we focus on, where we can optimize the assets using our vertical integration and scale to meaningfully increase free cash flow for shareholders."

Acquisition Highlights

  • Net production of ~68 Mboepd (409 MMcfepd)(a)
    • ~35% production increase to standalone Diversified(a)
    • ~70% liquids and ~30% natural gas(a)
  • Gross purchase price of ~$1,800 million with a purchase price multiple of ~3.3x on NTM Adjusted EBITDA(b)
    • Gross purchase price adjusted by customary amounts including interim cash flows and working capital liabilities; minimal DEC liquidity required at closing
    • Estimated NTM Adjusted EBITDA of ~$548 million(b), before anticipated synergies
  • PDP reserves of ~1,168 Bcfe(c) and PV-10 of ~$2.0 billion(d) 

ABS Issuance Highlights

  • $1,455 million ABS notes structured as a master trust; Acquisition closing directly into the ABS eliminated the need for an acquisition bridge facility, reducing financing costs
  • Anchored by funds managed by The Carlyle Group “Carlyle”, through the Company’s strategic partnership with Carlyle, which was expanded to up to $10 billion of growth capital at the announcement of the Acquisition
  • The A tranche notes priced at a blended coupon of 6.84%, benefited by an investment-grade rating

2026 Impact

  • Birch is expected to add ~$50 million of Adjusted EBITDA to Q4 2026 results

Doug Kris dkris@dgoc.com

Adjusted EBITDA

As used herein, EBITDA represents earnings before interest, taxes, depletion, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA includes adjustments for items that are not comparable period-over-period, namely, finance costs, accretion of asset retirement obligation, other (income) expense, (gain) loss  on fair value adjustments of unsettled financial instruments, (gain) loss on natural gas and oil property and equipment, (gain) loss on sale of equity interest, unrealized (gain) loss on investment, costs associated with acquisitions, other adjusting costs, loss on early retirement of debt, non-cash equity compensation, (gain) loss on interest rate swaps, and items of a similar nature.

Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for operating profit or loss, net income or loss, or cash flows provided by operating, investing and financing activities. Reconciling items in future periods could be significant.

PV-10

PV-10 is a non-GAAP financial measure that differs from a financial measure under GAAP known as "standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows" in that PV-10 is calculated without including future income taxes and discounted at 10 percent. The Company believes the presentation of PV-10 provides useful information because it is widely used by investors in evaluating oil and natural gas companies without regard to specific income tax characteristics of such entities. PV-10 is not intended to represent the current market value of the Company's estimated proved reserves. PV-10 should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the standardized measure as defined under GAAP.

data.title: Anthropic's blockbuster debut tests Wall Street's faith in AI boom
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

The early exuberance faded, however, signaling volatility ahead as investors locked in quick gains and the main indexes retreated amid renewed jitters over the sector's outlook.

Shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company opened at $111.50, which was 34% higher than the IPO price of $83. But the stock pared gains and was last trading around $99.

Anthropic's fully diluted $2 trillion valuation includes stock options and restricted stock units that the company has promised employees but which have not been vested into actual shares. Based on Anthropic's outstanding shares, the company's value reached as much as $1.5 trillion on Thursday, on par with Tesla.

The AI market euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks, with last week's resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang causing concern. The technology has boosted economic growth but has prompted unease about mounting debt loads and doomsday warnings. An anti-data-center movement may have helped Democrats sweep the US midterm elections.

"The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," said Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. "We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability."

The six-year-old company has positioned itself as the gatekeeper of AI safety while selling investors the idea that it can be profitable despite massive compute costs. Led by Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has also signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Amodei told CNBC in an interview on Thursday.

Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from the previous quarter, even as the pace of growth slowed sharply from the prior quarter. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google.

INDUSTRY BENCHMARK, EMPLOYEE PAYDAY

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show.

Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for the purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

Based on the IPO price, Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified over whether the AI boom is becoming a bubble as soaring valuations and a web of circular deals involving AI developers, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors fuel questions about the durability of the industry's growth.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far insulated it from these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

Anthropic "isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," said Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group. "History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon."

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

The massive IPO will earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

data.title: Software-Defined Vehicles Market to Reach USD 310.46 Billion by 2035, Growing at 20.74% CAGR

PUNE, India, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- According to Market Growth Reports, The global Software-Defined Vehicles Market is projected to grow from USD 56.94 billion to USD 310.46 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 20.74%. Increasing demand for connected vehicles, advanced driver assistance systems, electric vehicles, and software-based automotive technologies is creating new opportunities for vehicle manufacturers and technology providers worldwide.

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is experiencing significant transformation as automotive manufacturers shift from traditional hardware-focused vehicle development toward software-controlled vehicle platforms. Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) allow manufacturers to introduce new features, improve vehicle performance, enhance safety, and update digital systems without requiring major physical modifications.

The growing integration of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, vehicle connectivity, and over-the-air software updates is accelerating the adoption of software-defined vehicle technologies. Automakers are increasingly investing in centralized computing platforms, advanced operating systems, and intelligent electronic architectures to improve vehicle functionality and deliver better driving experiences.

Browse more information and get a free sample PDF of the research report: https://www.marketgrowthreports.com/market-reports/software-defined-vehicles-market-125859

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Overview

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is becoming an important part of the global automotive industry's digital transformation. Modern vehicles increasingly depend on software to manage essential functions, including navigation, entertainment, battery management, vehicle diagnostics, driver assistance, and connected services.

Unlike conventional vehicles, which rely heavily on separate electronic control units, software-defined vehicles use more integrated computing systems and centralized software platforms. This approach helps automotive manufacturers reduce system complexity, improve software management, and introduce new vehicle capabilities throughout the product lifecycle.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Growth Drivers

One of the major factors supporting Software-Defined Vehicles Market growth is the increasing adoption of connected automotive technologies. Consumers expect modern vehicles to provide smartphone integration, real-time navigation, digital entertainment, remote access, and advanced safety features.

The expansion of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) is another important growth factor. Software-defined vehicle platforms support technologies such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, automated emergency braking, driver monitoring, and intelligent parking assistance. Automotive manufacturers are investing in artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve vehicle decision-making and support more advanced driving capabilities. These technologies process information from cameras, radar, sensors, and other vehicle systems to enhance driving safety and operational performance.

Over-the-air software updates are also transforming the automotive industry. Manufacturers can remotely introduce security improvements, fix software issues, and add selected vehicle features without requiring customers to visit service centers. Furthermore, the growing focus on electric mobility, digital vehicle services, and centralized automotive computing is encouraging partnerships between automobile manufacturers, semiconductor companies, cloud service providers, and software developers.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Trends

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is witnessing rapid technological changes as automotive companies introduce advanced software architectures and intelligent vehicle platforms. A major trend is the transition toward centralized and zonal computing architectures. These systems help manufacturers manage multiple vehicle functions through fewer, more powerful computing platforms, reducing dependence on numerous independent control units. Another important trend is the integration of artificial intelligence into automotive software. AI-powered systems support predictive maintenance, intelligent navigation, driver behavior analysis, and improved vehicle diagnostics.

Cybersecurity is becoming increasingly important as connected vehicles exchange information with external networks. Manufacturers are strengthening software security, data protection, and vehicle communication systems to reduce digital risks. The expansion of vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is also attracting industry attention. This technology allows vehicles to exchange information with transportation infrastructure, other vehicles, and connected systems, supporting safer and more efficient mobility. Additionally, manufacturers are exploring subscription-based software features and digital services that can create ongoing revenue opportunities after the initial vehicle purchase.

Software-Defined Vehicles Market Segmentation Analysis

The Software-Defined Vehicles Market is segmented by vehicle type and application, reflecting the growing use of software technologies across different automotive platforms.

       Nov 19 (Reuters) - MSCI's index of Latin American equities slipped to a one-year low on Thursday amid fragile global sentiment, while growing expectations of tighter US interest rates weighed on regional currencies.‌
    The index fell 2.72% to its weakest since late November 2025.
    "These don't seem like fundamental bottom-up moves. It seems like short-term macro sentiment, which is creating high levels of correlation across different asset classes," said Malcolm Dorson, head of EM strategy at Global X.
     "Fed governors, including Governor Waller, have said inflation remains heading in the wrong direction. So it's not just emerging markets. Risk assets in general have been on edge."
    Brazil's benchmark Bovespa index fell 1% as losses in the energy sector weighedon the benchmark.
    Investors also assessed the Brazil Senate's approval of a fiscal package aimed at meeting the government's fiscal targets, although many viewed the measures as only an initial step toward improving the country's debt outlook.
    Brazilian President Lula da Silva criticized market participants for profiting from speculation over his cabinet picks. Brazilian assets have sold off since his reelection.
     Brazil's real slipped 0.9% to a fresh April 2025 low.
     The broader index of Latin American currencies fell 1.96% to a 10- month low.
    Investors have largely priced in a quarter-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve in December, helping lift the dollar to multi-month highs and putting pressure on emerging-market currencies across the board.
    A stronger dollar weighs on developing-market currencies by drawing capital into US assets and away from riskier markets.‌
    In Mexico, the peso fell 1.5% against the US dollar as investors weighed the widening monetary policy divergence between the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Mexico after the Fed raised interest rates in September for the first time in three years, while Banxico delivered a quarter-percentage-point rate cut earlier this month.

data.title: US court ruling jeopardizes Sentinel Midstream's license for deepwater oil export project
data.description:
* Court says Texas GulfLink application area overlapped Enterprise's SPOT project area

* Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward, source says

* Sentinel cannot continue with the current license, source says

* Company expects construction schedule to proceed as planned

By Arathy Somasekhar

HOUSTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - A court ruling has jeopardized a license for Sentinel Midstream's $2.1 billion deepwater crude oil export project off the Texas coast, an environmental group that petitioned the court said this week.

The ruling, which took effect on October 30, poses a setback and likely delays for the oil transportation and storage company, which has already started work on the project. It could also impact other pending deepwater port applications.

In August, a US appeals court voided a federal record of decision for Sentinel Midstream's Texas GulfLink project, citing overlap with another deepwater project.

An official at Sentinel Midstream said work would continue on the project, characterizing it as "business as usual." But a source with knowledge of the situation said the company could not continue with the offshore project on the current license.

Last year, the US Maritime Administration (MARAD), in its record of decision (ROD), approved Texas GulfLink with conditions and the company received its license in January 2026. President Donald Trump has pushed for faster project approvals to bolster the US energy industry. Sentinel made a final investment decision in May and began construction.

MARAD's record of decision approving Texas GulfLink's application violated the Deepwater Port Act's requirement that only one deepwater port be approved per application area, the 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals said. Texas GulfLink's application area, when properly designated, would have intersected with Enterprise Products Partners' Sea Port Oil Terminal (SPOT) deepwater project.

Congress has struck a careful balance between promoting and regulating the construction and operation of deepwater ports, the court said, holding that the Deepwater Port Act requires an application area to encompass the entirety of a proposed deepwater port site, including any proposed pipeline.

"The Court's decision is clear: it vacated the record of decision that was the foundation of GulfLink's license. Now, MARAD has to revoke or suspend that license," Michael Brown, a counsel for the petitioners, said on Wednesday.

Construction of the project cannot continue without a federal deepwater port license, said environmental group Better Brazoria Clean Air and Water in a press release this week.

MARAD said it was disappointed with the outcome and continues to pursue all avenues to achieve the President's vision of American energy dominance.

"Sentinel is working with MARAD to discuss its options for moving forward. The company cannot continue with the current license," a source familiar with the matter said.

In comments to Reuters this week, Sentinel said its license has not been suspended or terminated.

Texas GulfLink, to be situated about 30 miles off Freeport, Texas, remains on track for a fourth-quarter 2028 operational date, Bruce Heine, a senior vice president at Sentinel, said this week, adding that given the narrow nature and scope of the issue, there are multiple paths to address the statutory concern without disrupting ongoing construction activities or overall project schedule.

"It remains business as usual for Texas GulfLink, with site development and improvement activities currently underway at our Jones Creek onshore terminal facility as we prepare to commence tank construction," Heine said, adding that major long-lead equipment and pipe have been purchased, and key construction contracts executed.

However, the company in its motion last month to stay the court mandate said that the Texas GulfLink's license expressly incorporates the ROD as a compliance standard, adding that voiding the ROD in turn exposed the license to suspension or revocation by MARAD, and prevents construction of offshore components.

"At a minimum, the cloud on Texas GulfLink's regulatory posture will harm Texas GulfLink in the marketplace," the company said then, adding that "given the uncertainty of its ROD and license, Texas GulfLink will not commence construction of the deepwater port under the current posture, even if the mandate is stayed."

Texas GulfLink plans to petition the Supreme Court, the company said in its motion. It added that there are two other pending deepwater ports under review with application areas similar to Texas GulfLink's that will likely require redesignation as a result of the panel's decision, potentially resulting in consequential impacts to those projects as well.

If Sentinel is required to resubmit its application, it would have to await a new ROD and license. While it took nearly seven years for Sentinel to secure approvals last time, MARAD has sped up its approval process under US President Donald Trump. It recently issued a deepwater project application license in just 410 days, nearly 3.7 years faster than ​the historical average.

The Texas GulfLink project aims to fully load a supertanker with about 2 million barrels of oil per day. The administration in recent weeks also approved deepwater port license applications for Energy Transfer's Blue Marlin Offshore Port, an oil export project off the Louisiana coast, and for ST LNG, which aims to ship liquefied natural gas off ​the Texas coast.

(Reporting by Arathy Somasekhar in Houston; additional reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Liz Hampton and David Gregorio)

data.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months-committee
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday.

The approvals for 879,000 chip shipmentsby the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said. Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million of them to China total during the period, committee documents show.

The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which fueled renewed calls for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats.

All four of the Chinese companies highlighted in the committee report are on the Pentagon list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.

The committee chair, Brian Mast, has "exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD's AI chip licenses for the People's Republic of China," the committee said in a statement. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipment of the chips, which included Nvidia's ( NVDA ) H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China."

AMD did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Wall Street slides as Anthropic's debut fails to revive AI enthusiasm
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - US stocks slumped on Thursday as Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revive faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its share price ebbed.

At last glance, Anthropic shares were 14.3% above the offer price. All three major US stock indexes were off more than 1%, with the benchmark S&P 500 on track to log its fifth straight session of losses.

Anthropic's debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced late Wednesday at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly before noon. After the company's market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began to ebb.

"The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri. "That money is coming from somewhere; investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from today's trading behavior, whether it's up or down."

Even so, Ellerbroek's enthusiasm for the AI trade has waned.

"My beliefs about the growth in data center capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two," he added. "Nvidia's ( NVDA ) crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact."

"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly."

Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) shares tumbled 9.2% after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most tech stocks were lower, with Micron and Broadcom ( AVGO ) down between 1.1% and 2.0%.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) declined 1.7% after five straight sessions of losses through Wednesday, when its upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dipped 1.5%.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius were down 5.0% and 7.8%, respectively.

The broader technology sector slid 1.3%.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) shares jumped 5.9% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance.

Walmart ( WMT ) was down 1% following the retail giant's disappointing annual sales forecast.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 900.74 points, or 1.79%, to 49,298.08, the S&P 500 lost 112.51 points, or 1.54%, to 7,211.12 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 391.11 points, or 1.60%, to 24,038.78.

FOCUS TURNS TO THE FED

Following Wednesday's release of minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in a 94.1% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the central bank's December meeting, with a small but growing 5.9% chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above the central bank's average annual 2% target.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 16 new highs and 668 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,148 stocks rose and 3,518 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.06-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted one new 52-week high and 16 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 25 new highs and 438 new lows.

(Reporting by Stephen Culp; Additional reporting by Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur in Bengaluru; Editing by David Gregorio)

Nov 19 - Britain's FTSE 100 index hit a six-week low on Thursday in a broad risk off move led by losses in defensive stocks, while Anthropic surged in its hotly anticipated Nasdaq debut.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 ended down 0.9% at 10,452.68 points. The midcap FTSE 250 index closed 0.7% lower in its six straight session of declines, its longest string of losses in a year.

* Defensive corners of the market were the main drag: Unilever ( UL ) fell 2.2%, National Grid lost 2.6% and Vodafone Group ( VOD ) dropped 4.0%

* Also dragging were HSBC Holdings ( HSBC ) which fell 0.9%, GSK lost 1.7% and Shell eased 0.6%

* Anthropic soared in its Nasdaq debut after London markets closed with its market value hitting as high as $2.1 trillion as investors rushed to buy shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company

* London stocks were already trading lower ahead of the hotly anticipated IPO while the stellar debut failed to quell investor worries over AI trade

* Markets will also be watching developments around a proposed UK-EU "trusted partnership", seen as key to securing 'Made in Europe' status for British vehicles

* In company news, Babcock International ( BCKIF ) jumped 9.4% to the top of the FTSE 100 after the defence engineering group posted a 13% increase in first-half underlying operating profit

* Merchant banking group Close Brothers slid 7.7% to lead midcap decliners after the lender said it expects a further modest decline in net interest margin for the rest of fiscal year 2027

* Decliners outnumbered advancers by a 2.0-to-1 margin in the London market digest.

(Reporting by Darshan Kumar and Medha Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: California faces mounting deficit and AI bubble risks, analyst warns
data.description:
Despite a recent AI-fueled revenue surge, California remains ill-prepared for a potential economic downturn or stock market correction the Legislative Analyst’s Office said in its independent assessment of the state’s fiscal outlook Wednesday.

The LAO delivers a fiscal outlook to state lawmakers annually ahead of the governor’s budget introduction in January.

Although high-tech gains have buoyed general fund collections in the short term, Legislative Analyst Gabriel Petek said the state has an underlying structural imbalance. 

California faces a $2 billion deficit at the end of 2027-28 — which Petek described as “modest” compared to last year’s projected $18 billion deficit — but long-term shortfalls could expand significantly if market volatility persists, according to the LAO’s November fiscal report.

“The state is facing a budget deficit for the fifth year in a row despite being at record revenue levels,” Petek said during the briefing. “The budget problem for the first year is fairly small, but grows to $30 billion by 2028-29.”

The primary concern is California’s reliance on personal income tax revenues derived from capital gains and stock market performance, Petek said. With stock indexes up substantially since 2022, indicators — such as margin debt and price-to-earnings ratios — match levels not seen since the dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, he said.

“The theme of this report is the stock market is a looming risk to this budget,” Petek said. 

“The stock market has been booming since 2022,” he said. “We have seen the stock market go up by 150%. State income tax revenues have grown at twice the normal rate. It’s been a good run.”

The problem is that everything the LAO’s office is tracking in terms of economic indicators show the stock market has moved into “classic speculative bubble territory,” Petek said.

While baseline estimates show near-term revenues up by $11 billion over June projections, constitutional spending mandates — such as Proposition 98 school funding and Proposition 2 reserve requirements — offset those gains, Petek said. Fast-growing state commitments in Health and Human Services, including In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS), Medi-Cal, and childcare, continue to put ongoing pressure on the budget, he said.

To illustrate the severity of a potential crash scenario reminiscent of the 2001 or 2008 downturns, legislative analysts modeled a severe market drop by 2027, Petek said. Under that scenario, state revenues could fall $130 billion below baseline projections, creating annual budget deficits near $35 billion, he said.

Addressing a shortfall of that magnitude under a severe recession would require drastic measures, he said.

Generating $50 billion in solutions would be akin to the Legislature undoing virtually all discretionary service expansions enacted since 2019, or enacting tax increases larger than recent ballot measures, Petek said.

To safeguard California’s fiscal position ahead of the governor's budget proposal in January, the Legislative Analyst’s Office urged lawmakers to adopt prudent revenue assumptions, maximize reserves, and focus on structural fixes rather than reliance on temporary maneuvers.

“Our central message is the state budget is overextended at this point,” Petek stated. “We think the Legislature should seek to right-size the budget rather than covering it through one-time maneuvers.”

data.title: EXPLAINER-Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?
data.description:
(Adds details on Alice Huang, possible state and SEC actions)

By Tom Hals

WILMINGTON, Delaware, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Reports that Jensen Huang, the co-founder of AI chip powerhouse Nvidia ( NVDA ), had an extramarital affair with a company executive and ties to a suspected Chinese spy have led to his resignation as CEO and sparked investigations by the US securities regulator and FBI, calls for congressional hearings, a review by the company's independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit.

Below is a look at the potential legal exposure for Huang, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and the directors of the company, which dominates the global market for computer chips that power the AI economy.

WHAT ARE THE ALLEGATIONS?

Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of ​Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and US intelligence agencies are trying to determine her ties to China's Ministry of State Security, according to two people familiar with the matter. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) advanced AI chips that are subject to US export restrictions.

Huang admitted he was unfaithful to his wife without providing details about the relationship, which led to a drop in Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock price. US President Donald Trump said Huang told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy and Huang has not been accused of criminal wrongdoing.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China's foreign ministry has said was "groundless."

Nvidia ( NVDA ) formed an independent committee of directors that hired the Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to assist in an internal investigation.

Huang resigned on November 11 after reports that he had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) sits at the center of the ​technological rivalry between the United States and China. Washington has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since ​2022. News of the affair has emerged as Democrats seized control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, propelled in part by anti-AI and anti-corruption sentiment.

WHAT ABOUT FEDERAL SECURITIES FRAUD?

A proposed class action was filed in San Jose, California, federal court on November 9 alleging the company and Huang defrauded shareholders by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which Jensen Huang described in an October 30 Bloomberg interview as "normal and not unusual."

Securities fraud plaintiffs must show that Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Huang knowingly misled investors, that investors relied on those misleading statements and that those misleading statements artificially inflated the stock.

The lawsuit did not specify damages but the stock lost around 20% from its peak to the end of the class period, a decline of around $1 trillion in market value.

Such lawsuits are often filed in the wake of a company's stock suffering a large drop, and more are likely.

While the vast majority of US public companies have insurance against securities lawsuits, Nvidia ( NVDA ) does not given its huge financial resources.

WHAT ABOUT STATE LAW VIOLATIONS?

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, a Republican, is investigating whether Huang's actions harmed state pension funds and her office said they were looking at it through a consumer protection lens focused on potential misrepresentations.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bloomberg that the Nvidia ( NVDA ) crisis raised red flags and his office could investigate. Bonta's office did not respond to a request for further details.

State officials could use state securities laws to pursue investigations of alleged violations, according to legal experts. New York's Martin Act is considered the most powerful and the state's attorneys general have used it to police Wall Street, including an insider trading case brought this year. The Martin Act also allows the attorney general to pursue criminal claims.

No states have brought claims and the New York attorney general did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

COULD THE SEC STEP IN?

The US Securities and Exchange Commission launched a civil investigation that included whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the situation. Reuters has not verified the report.

The regulator would have a lower burden of proof than a private investor class action and the SEC can obtain alternative remedies, such as barring individuals from serving as officers or directors of public companies.

In 2022, during the administration of Democratic President Joe Biden, Nvidia ( NVDA ) settled allegations by the SEC that in 2018 it had made inadequate disclosures regarding the growth of its processors for the gaming market. The company paid a $5.5 million fine but did not admit or deny the allegations. An investor class action lawsuit over the same allegations is ongoing.

The SEC declined to comment.

COULD THE BOARD BE HELD LIABLE?

An investor filed a so-called derivative lawsuit on November 11 seeking to hold the board liable for failing to make a good faith effort to oversee the business and Huang. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia ( NVDA ) to make repeated assurances about the company's dealings with Megaspeed and the board did not act on warning signs about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang until it was public.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in the Northern District of California, also said the board lacked independence to investigate Huang.

Huang's resignation could strengthen the board's defenses against derivative lawsuits by showing the directors were acting on signs of misconduct by forcing him out and refusing to consider his return.

Investors, including state pension funds, can also use their shareholder rights to seek internal records to investigate the board and look for potential conflicts.

The board could sue Huang for any fines or securities fraud settlements that result from the scandal. For example, electric truck maker Nikola took legal action and got a judgment of $168 million against its former CEO Trevor Milton.

CAN SECURITIES FRAUD CARRY CRIMINAL PENALTIES?

Only a small fraction of all securities fraud cases lead to criminal charges, as most violations are handled through civil or administrative enforcement.

But a federal statute, enacted as part of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, criminalizes schemes that knowingly defraud investors through false pretenses. Prosecutors would need to show that Huang intentionally lied to the public about the affair in order to keep Nvidia's ( NVDA ) stock price from falling, rather than for personal reasons such as avoiding embarrassment.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche also said the FBI was investigating if Alice Huang was a spy.

If Huang knew about Alice Huang's alleged intelligence connection, he could face criminal liability under the Economic Espionage Act, a 1996 law that punishes the misappropriation of trade secrets to benefit a foreign government.

(Reporting by Tom Hals in Wilmington, Delaware; Additional reporting by Jan Wolfe and Steve Holland; Editing by Nick Zieminski and Noleen Walder)

data.title: License information for AI chips sent to China released by US House committee
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday. 

The approvals included 75,000 semiconductors for Alibaba ( BABA ), 150,000 for Tencent ( TCTZF ), 43,000 for Baidu ( BIDU ), and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said. 

Its chair, Brian Mast, has "exercised his authorities under the Export Control Reform Act to publicly reveal export control license application information regarding NVIDIA and AMD's AI chip licenses for the People's Republic of China," the committee said in a statement. 

The committee said that its findings included "requested sales of 3.4 million AI chips to China, and the approval of more than 879,000 by BIS, including approvals for AI chip exports to Department of War-designated Chinese Military Companies like Alibaba ( BABA ) and Tencent ( TCTZF )."

(Reporting by Alexandra Alper, Ryan Patrick Jones, Katharine Jackson; editing by Scott Malone and Chris Sanders)
